name: Crew Endurance Team (Nita Lewis Shattuck, PhD; Panagiotis Matsangas, PhD)
org: Naval Postgraduate School, Human Systems Integration / Operations Research
why: Team runs long-duration wearable sleep studies on ships: May 2026 Aerosp Med Hum Perform paper tracked 99 US Navy surface warfare officers with wearables for a median 340 days; 2026 Sleep RCT used wrist actigraphs on watch schedules; Navy/DVIDS report a planned ring-based study on Coast Guard icebreaker Healy (sleep, HR, HRV, SpO2, skin temp), and their findings underpin the Navy's Comprehensive Crew Endurance Management Policy.
why_now: Two 2026 papers (Sleep, Apr 2026; Aerosp Med Hum Perform, May 2026) on wearable-measured sleep at sea.
ask: Offer 5-10 DevKits for a comparison against their current ring/watch devices on a shore-based or underway cohort.
opener: Hi Dr. Shattuck, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. Your 340-day wearable sleep work with surface warfare officers is the longest field dataset I've seen. We're building a screenless band worn overnight (sleep and HRV, open SDK, raw data access). Would a few DevKits be useful as a comparison device in a future cohort? I'd value 15 minutes on what your team needs from a device.

name: SWIFT: Shiftwork in Firefighters study (Nicole P. Bowles, PhD)
org: Oregon Health & Science University, Oregon Institute of Occupational Health Sciences
why: SWIFT compares 24/48 vs 1/3/2/3 firefighter schedules with actigraphy, chest-strap heart rate and vigilance tests over 14 days, built with unions and fire leadership in Oregon and Utah (186 firefighters to date per OHSU). July 2026 Nat Sci Sleep paper used actigraphy from 120 SWIFT firefighters (2,617 observations).
why_now: Nature and Science of Sleep paper published 2026-07-10.
ask: Offer DevKits so a SWIFT follow-up can capture overnight HRV alongside actigraphy without a chest strap.
opener: Hi Dr. Bowles, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. SWIFT pairing actigraphy with a chest strap across shift schedules is exactly the data problem we're building for: a screenless band worn overnight that records sleep and HRV with an open SDK. Would DevKits be useful in a follow-up wave? I'd value 15 minutes on what firefighters will and won't wear.
